_note: probe_trawler_bulwark with the bow closed by the 45 degree wall. Bow is -Z; hull_28x10 has beam_m 10 and bow_taper_m = beam_m * 0.5 = 5, so the deck tapers over z=0..5, the port stem is the line x+z=5, the starboard stem x-z=5, and the stem head is (5, 0). Walls 4/5 run '+x-z' and '-x-z' from the shoulders along those stems; walls 6/7 are the same runs as cap rail (height 0.09, thickness 0.5 = a horizontal plank, the trick decks cannot do on a diagonal) and carry the deck colour explicitly so they merge into the existing bucket. GEOMETRY, all of it solved from beam_m and bow_taper_m rather than nudged: with T = bow_taper_m = 5, deck-edge inset i = 0.1 (the inset walls 1/2 already use: face at x=0.1) and thickness t = 0.2, a run's centreline sits c = i + t/2 = 0.2 m in from the edge, so the port centreline is x+z = T + c*sqrt(2) = 5.28284 and the starboard x-z = T - c*sqrt(2) = 4.71716. They cross at (T, c*sqrt(2)) = (5, 0.28284) — 0.28284 m aft of the stem head, because two lines each inset c from a 90 degree apex meet c*sqrt(2) behind it. Crossing the centrelines is NOT closure: a run's end face is square to its own run, so covering the last station of the OPPOSITE stem needs the end face carried to that stem line, which is a further c past the crossing. Length is therefore (T - c) * sqrt(2) [shoulder mitre to crossing] + c [crossing to the opposite stem] + 0.1 [overlap aft past the shoulder mitre, so the joint is a lap not a knife edge] + 0.02 [protrusion past the opposite stem, so the last station is covered by a measurable margin instead of by an exact tie] = 6.78823 + 0.2 + 0.1 + 0.02 = 7.10823. Walls 6/7 are the same construction with c = i + 0.5/2 = 0.35: (T - 0.35) * sqrt(2) + 0.35 + 0.1 + 0.02 = 7.04609. Start points are the mitres with walls 1/2 and decks 20/21 backed off 0.1 along the run: (0.2, 5.08284) -> (0.12929, 5.15355) and (0.35, 5.14497) -> (0.27929, 5.21569). MEASURED, on the colliders StructureBaker actually emits (exact ray-vs-box against the ideal outline, no sampled step to hide a thin hole behind; 20001 stations per stem from the stem head to the shoulder, plus 4001 on the straight side aft of it): 0 stations lack a bulwark within 0.8 m inboard, port and starboard, forward of the shoulder and aft of it. The previous version of this fixture left 118/20001 stations per stem bare over z=0..0.02929 — 0.04142 m of open deck edge on each stem, a 0.0828 m aperture across the stem head — while this note claimed it was 'sub-centimetre short'. That claim was false. What is true and still open: at mid-stem the run is solid from 0.1000 to 0.3000 m inboard of the deck edge and the cap rail from 0.1000 to 0.6000, matching walls 1/2 and decks 20/21 exactly; the two end faces overhang the opposite stem line by 0.0200 m (measured 0.0200 at (5.0849, 0.0566)), which is the only geometry in the plan outside the ideal deck outline; and a 0.142 m deep pocket of open deck remains forward of the bulwark at the stem head, measured on the centreline, because two faces inset 0.1 m from a 90 degree apex cannot meet closer than i*sqrt(2) = 0.1414 m behind it — it is enclosed by the two runs and the hull sides, not an aperture. Height 1.1, thickness 0.2 and inset 0.1 are still hand-numbers that only suit a 10 m beam. Everything else is the probe fixture verbatim; both still bake to 4 mesh instances.
